## Where the day goes

Summary statistics are easy; *defensible* summary statistics presented well are not.
Today is about the gap between the two.

## Sessions

| # | Session | Material |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Publication tables with `gt` and `gtsummary` | [`scripts/gt-summary-tables.R`](scripts/gt-summary-tables.R), [`scripts/gt-tables-basics.R`](scripts/gt-tables-basics.R) |
| 2 | ggplot2 from the grammar up | [`scripts/nhanes-ggplot-basics.R`](scripts/nhanes-ggplot-basics.R) |
| 3 | Live indicator data: WDI and OWID | [`scripts/wdi-indicators.R`](scripts/wdi-indicators.R), [`scripts/owid-tutorial.R`](scripts/owid-tutorial.R) |
| 4 | Chart critique and redesign | [`scripts/gt-bar-defence.R`](scripts/gt-bar-defence.R) |

## Scripts in this folder

- `10-useful-commands.R` — the dplyr verbs you will reach for every day
- `birthweight-pregnancy.R` — a worked EDA on health data
- `nhanes-ggplot-advanced.R` — facets, scales, annotation, themes

## A note on API sessions

`wdi-indicators.R` and `owid-tutorial.R` hit live APIs. If the room's connection is
unreliable, run them before the session and cache the result; the OWID script includes
fallback approaches for when the primary endpoint is down.

## What you should be able to do by 16:30

- produce a formatted table you would put in a paper, from raw data, in under ten lines
- choose a chart type by asking what comparison the reader must make
- pull an indicator series for any country from the World Bank without leaving R
- say what is wrong with a bad chart in specific terms
